items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

bears: Capex of $195–205B this year has pushed free cash flow negative
Debt and equity raising to fund AI build-out
Chart broke support; some traders are calling for $250 if capex rises again
bulls: Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter with a $514B backlog
TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia
Stock looks oversold (RSI near 30) at about 24x forward earnings
items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

bears: About $220B of capex this year weighs on free cash flow
Reports of GPUs sitting idle in warehouses feed bubble talk

bulls: AWS growth has sped up five quarters in a row, to 36.7% last quarter
AWS capacity is reported sold out through 2026
Stock is about 13% off its August high at about 24x next year's earnings
items.name: Amazon
items.street: Strong Buy from 60 analysts; average target about $331, about a third above Friday's $248 close. The number everyone is watching is AWS growth (30–35% expected).
items.take: Retail traders are more upbeat on Amazon than on Alphabet going into earnings. Your call is about $12 below its $260 strike; AWS growth vs. the 30–35% range is the swing factor.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

items.name: Occidental Petroleum
items.about: Occidental is a US oil and gas producer with chemicals and carbon-capture businesses.
items.why: Energy shares rose on Friday as oil kept climbing, and OXY closed at $64.00, up 1.6%. Posts say most of the day's options premium was in calls and that Iran-deal headlines are the swing factor for crude; an OPEC+ decision over the weekend to hold December targets steady was also cited in the stream.

items.name: TG Therapeutics
items.about: TG Therapeutics is a biotech whose main product is Briumvi for relapsing multiple sclerosis.
items.why: The stock jumped 5.3% to a new high near $61.76 and topped the board. Posts say traders are positioning ahead of Q3 earnings, a subcutaneous Briumvi Phase 3 readout (the company has guided to around year-end or early 2027) and unconfirmed Sanofi buyout speculation; one post cites a $72 JPMorgan target, which is unverified.

items.name: VanEck Gold Miners ETF
items.about: GDX is an ETF that holds large gold-mining companies.
items.why: The fund fell 5.2% as gold slid about 3.5% to multi-month lows, according to posts, and miners fell harder than the metal. Chart-focused posts describe the move as oversold, while others point to rising rates, a firmer dollar and Treasury issuance as pressures.

items.name: Affirm Holdings
items.about: Affirm offers buy-now-pay-later loans at online and in-store checkout.
items.why: Affirm slipped 1.8% on a down day for growth names. Posts say it reports fiscal Q1 results Thursday after the close, with guidance implying revenue-less-transaction-costs growth of roughly 26% to 30% versus 39% last quarter; one post also flags insider selling.

items.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund
items.about: XLV is an ETF that tracks the health care stocks in the S&P 500.
items.why: Health care held up while technology fell, and posts say the fund is on track for its best October ever relative to SPY (about 11 points of outperformance). Regeneron's strong Q3 report, which sent it up more than 11% on Friday, and gains in Eli Lilly and J&J were cited.

items.name: Exxon Mobil
items.about: Exxon Mobil is the largest US integrated oil and gas company.
items.why: Exxon rose 2.2% to its highest close in about a month after Q3 results. Posts say adjusted refining earnings of $9.05 billion exceeded upstream at $7.31 billion, net debt fell by more than $9 billion, and the company reaffirmed buybacks; options flow was described as mixed.

items.name: Vermilion Energy
items.about: Vermilion Energy is a Canadian oil and gas producer with significant European natural-gas exposure.
items.why: The stock rose 1.3% alongside energy peers. Posts say European gas prices jumped about 6% and that QatarEnergy extended force majeure on LNG deliveries through December; neither claim is confirmed here.

items.name: Direxion Daily Junior Gold Miners Bull 2X
items.about: JNUG is a leveraged ETF that seeks twice the daily return of a junior gold miners index.
items.why: The 2x fund lost 11.8% as junior gold miners fell with gold, and its high retail watcher count (about 79,000) reflects heavy dip interest in the posts. Daily-reset leverage magnifies moves in both directions.

items.name: Precigen
items.about: Precigen is a biotech whose gene therapy Papzimeos treats recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.
items.why: PGEN closed up 4.5% at $6.94, but a Stocktwits news item reports it fell about 27% after hours when the FDA granted accelerated approval to rival Inovio's competing RRP drug (PDUFA date was Oct 30). Posts say Precigen reports Q3 earnings Wednesday.

items.name: ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ
items.about: SQQQ is a leveraged ETF that seeks three times the inverse daily return of the Nasdaq-100.
items.why: The fund gained 10.6%, which implies the Nasdaq-100 fell roughly 3.5% on Friday. Posts tie nervousness to Iran headlines (talks versus resumed strikes after Tuesday's midterms) and the rotation out of tech.

items.name: SPDR Gold Shares
items.about: GLD is an ETF backed by physical gold bullion.
items.why: Gold fell 3.5% to a multi-month low, per posts; spot gold was already near $4,000 an ounce in late October after a weekly decline. Posts cite higher rates, a firmer dollar and record Treasury auctions, and split between calls for further downside and oversold bounce arguments.

items.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
items.about: XLE is an ETF holding the energy companies in the S&P 500.
items.why: Energy gained 1.9% as money rotated out of tech, helped by Exxon and Chevron earnings. Posts say the Strait of Hormuz and Iran negotiations remain the main swing factors, and that OPEC+ will keep December targets unchanged; the Stocktwits sentiment reading itself is bearish.

items.name: Crocs
items.about: Crocs designs and sells casual footwear under the Crocs and HEYDUDE brands.
items.why: Shares were roughly flat on the day but are up about 26% over the week according to a post, and chatter is at an extreme level. No single confirmed catalyst appears in the stream; posts mention Q3 results, buybacks, put-heavy options flow and class-action notices.

items.name: AbbVie
items.about: AbbVie is a pharmaceutical company best known for Skyrizi, Rinvoq and Humira.
items.why: AbbVie rose 1.4% after Q3 results. Posts say revenue was $17.4 billion (+10%) with adjusted EPS of $3.82, Skyrizi sales of $5.8 billion, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $13.95 to $13.99; the stock is near a one-month high.

items.name: Barrick Mining
items.about: Barrick is one of the world's largest gold and copper miners.
items.why: Barrick fell 4.3% to roughly a one-month low as gold dropped. Posts say options premium was split between puts and calls, and chartists are watching whether gold miners fill open price gaps lower.

items.name: Cisco Systems
items.about: Cisco makes networking, security and collaboration hardware and software.
items.why: Cisco dropped 3.8% in the tech selloff, trading near its lowest in a month. Posts say it reports earnings on Nov 11, and debate centers on AI data-center networking competition and the AI-bubble comparison with 2000.

items.name: Chevron
items.about: Chevron is a major US integrated oil and gas company.
items.why: Chevron rose 1.8% to a one-month high after Q3 results. Posts say production was about 4 million barrels of oil equivalent per day with $16.6 billion of operating cash flow, and that its upstream still out-earns refining, unlike Exxon.

items.name: First Majestic Silver
items.about: First Majestic is a silver-mining company operating in Mexico and the US.
items.why: The stock fell 7% as silver dropped, and posts describe the $14 to $15 area as a level it is retesting. Options premium was reported as mostly calls, and sentiment is bullish despite the slide.

items.name: iShares Silver Trust
items.about: SLV is an ETF backed by physical silver.
items.why: Silver fell 5.7% in the metals selloff, and posts describe silver as down roughly 60% from the $120 peak in January. The stream is dominated by dip-buying talk, with some bearish targets near $35.

items.name: Helus Pharma
items.about: Helus Pharma is a clinical-stage biotech developing deuterated psychedelic medicines for mental-health conditions.
items.why: Shares eased 1.1% while posts anticipate Phase 3 topline data for HLP003 in major depression, which the company has guided to by year-end. Posts also mention Compass Pathways' earnings call on Nov 3 as a sector catalyst and a new independent board chair; timing remains unconfirmed.
